source.title: A Defense of the Quadratic Model
source.authors: Alexandru Meterez; Pranav Ajit Nair; Depen Morwani; Cengiz Pehlevan; S. Kakade; Alex Damian

record.tranche_reason: The study probes learning-rate and batch-size stability boundaries in local quadratic LLM training and reports where runs diverge.
record.gate_note: The study reports no CIFAR classification-error results, random-initialization comparison, or training-error measurements. Its stability results come from local quadratic proxies around EMA checkpoints, not ordinary end-to-end pretraining.
record.test_reason: The study measures divergence of fixed-curvature, frozen-preconditioner quadratic proxies around LLM checkpoints. These experiments do not measure V5's nonlinear loss recovery, evolving sharpness at the stability threshold during full-batch training, or divergence despite initially subthreshold sharpness. None of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' local-stability interpretation, but incompletely summarizes the paper. Their main conclusion is that LLM pretraining can be approximated locally by structured quadratic problems, sometimes for up to 10% of training. They interpret filtered proxy probes as showing stochastic stability boundaries at small batches and deterministic boundaries at large batches under cosine scheduling; constant-rate large-batch probes exhibit both.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes stability in local quadratic expansions of LLM checkpoints with a frozen preconditioner and preconditioned SGD; it does not reproduce the cited learning-rate phase or sharpness measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes the reported shape of the stability boundary: diagonal for B = 1 and 64, flat cutoff for B = 1024. The paper also notes that the constant-learning-rate B = 1024 case differs from the cosine schedule, but those additional Figure 16 patterns are not extracted as rows.

fits_no_version.finding: After sequence-outlier filtering, local quadratic probes show diagonal stability boundaries at B = 1 and 64 and a flat cutoff at B = 1024 under cosine scheduling. Halving the checkpoint learning rate is always stable, whereas the nominal recipe is not always stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Filtered, frozen-preconditioner quadratic proxies around 150M-transformer checkpoints exhibit batch-size-dependent local stability boundaries near the training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Without filtering the top 1% of sequence outliers, nearly all tested hyperparameters diverged after an outsized spike.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stability of frozen-preconditioner LLM quadratic proxies depends strongly on removing sequence outliers.

fits_no_version.finding: With constant learning rates, small-batch proxies remain near a stochastic boundary, while B = 1024 exhibits both stochastic and deterministic boundaries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The type of local quadratic stability boundary depends on both batch size and learning-rate schedule.

record.problems: Results are for one model scale, architecture, and optimizer, and the stability evidence uses local quadratic proxies rather than full nonlinear training. The text describes boundary shapes and selected cells but does not provide their exact divergence fractions in prose.
record.rows_left_out: No additional prose-reported outcomes for this claim version. Figure 7 contains individual heatmap cell fractions, but precise values are figure-only and are not reconstructed here.

untested.parts: All parts: CIFAR training classification error, corrupted labels, and size, duration or regularization effects.
All parts: teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, deep plain tanh networks and Fixup.
All parts: initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed and trainable depth.

Loss recovery above the initial linearized stability limit in wide squared-loss networks; curvature reduction during recovery; full-batch sharpness rising and hovering at the threshold while training loss falls; divergence despite initially subthreshold sharpness.
All parts: batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V5 verdicts. Failure to measure V5 is not evidence limiting or challenging it. The discussion reports progressive sharpening as cosine learning rates decay, but does not establish V5's full-batch threshold-hovering trajectory. Figure-only divergence fractions cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100; random or corrupted labels; model size and training duration effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks and the effect of depth or shortcuts on training error.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed, or trainable depth.

The study does not test wide networks trained with squared loss from initialization, transient loss increase followed by low training loss, or sharpness rising and hovering at the stability threshold. It tests local quadratic proxies of LLM training at saved checkpoints.
Batch normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: 150M transformer
rows.size_stated: 150M (non-embedding) parameters; 168M with embedding and unembedding matrices
rows.operation_detail: Preconditioned SGD on a local quadratic expansion with frozen Adam second-moment preconditioner; learning rate and batch size varied over a grid, with 10 shuffled-sequence seeds per setting.

conditions.value: 5 × 3 grid; batch size multiplier less than 1 was unavailable

rows.measure: Fraction of runs diverging across the learning-rate and batch-size multiplier grid.
rows.value: The stability boundary follows the diagonal line.
rows.note: The text describes the boundary across B = 1 checkpoints collectively; it does not give individual cell fractions in prose.
rows.check: The diagonal proxy-stability boundary does not establish V5. Specify that the top 1% of sequence outliers, ranked by preconditioned Gauss–Newton Frobenius norm, were filtered before these probes.
